title: Suriname: maroons, contract workers and many languages
goal: Report what historians and the press say about Suriname, with según and verbs like explicar que.
grammar: reported statements and citing sources with según

sections.title: Suriname: maroons, contract workers and many languages
body: In this lesson you read about Suriname: its languages, the maroons who escaped slavery and built free communities in the jungle, the workers who came from Asia after 1863, and Suriname today.

The grammar is one you know: reporting what a source says with *según*, *explicar que* and *informar de que*. The screens and instructions are in English; the readings are in Spanish. (Belize, Guyana and Suriname are not Spanish-speaking countries: their official languages are English and Dutch.)

items: I can report what a source says with *según*, *explicar que* and *informar de que*.
I can say which language is official in Suriname and which one people use to understand each other.
I can use the new words for maroons, plantations and abolition.
